text:
samira: Hi team — first day and my Buildkite run for `redwood/frontend-components` fails during checkout when it tries to update submodules. Error shows permission denied / 403 for `redwood/design-tokens`. Anyone know the onboarding wrinkle here?

buildkite-bot: Build #1 failed - step: checkout (exit code: 128)
```
Cloning into 'submodules/design-tokens'...
remote: Repository not found.
fatal: repository 'https://github.com/redwood/design-tokens/' not found
error: could not fetch submodule 'submodules/design-tokens'
```

marco: Welcome! This usually happens because the Buildkite GitHub App installation doesn't have access to the submodule repo, or the pipeline is using HTTPS and lacks credentials for private submodules. Did the submodule repo live in a different org or is it private?

samira: It's private and in the same org (redwood). I assumed checkout would inherit the same perms.

infra-jen: Because submodules are fetched by the agent, the agent needs auth for every repo referenced. Our usual options: (1) add the submodule repo to the Buildkite GitHub App installation (preferred), (2) add a read-only deploy key to the submodule repo and make it available to agents, or (3) use a machine token in pipeline secrets (not ideal for new hires).

ci-oncall-bot: Onboarding guidance: do NOT create long-lived personal tokens. Request eng-infra for a deploy key or have infra add the repo to the Buildkite app. See pinned onboarding checklist in #eng-infra.

marco: If you need a quick workaround to unblock development, we sometimes switch the pipeline to SSH checkout and install an infra-managed deploy key on the agent image, but that's a heavier change. Best is to add the repo to the app install.

samira: Who should I ping to add the repo to the app? I'm new and don't want to break org settings.

infra-jen: Ping @marco or @alex.p in DM with the repo name. I'll handle the app install change (it requires org admin consent) or add a deploy key if you prefer. If it's a one-off internal lib we can also vendor the submodule temporarily.

alex.p: FYI if your PR comes from a fork, Buildkite runs still run but GH Actions can be blocked for forks — so keep that in mind if you reproduce failures locally. For this, adding the repo to the Buildkite app will fix it for org PRs.

samira: Thanks, @infra-jen. I've DM'd the repo and marked this in my onboarding checklist. Will re-run after it's added.

infra-jen: Repo added to Buildkite app (redwood/design-tokens). Re-run when ready.

samira: Re-ran build  logs show submodule clone succeeded and pipeline continued. Thanks!

buildkite-bot: Build #1 (re-run) passed - steps: checkout, build, test :white_check_mark:
